_variant_note: Wave-4 filter-trap: customer asks for 'today's gold rate at 22 karat for my gold loan'. The customer says 22k, but gold rate at 24k is relevant for comparison — a 24k query returns a different market rate. Actually, the get_gold_rate tool returns a flat object (not an array) per purity_karat. So the filter trap is: querying purity_karat=22 only gives the 22k rate, hiding the 24k rate. A broader model queries BOTH 22k AND 24k rates to give a complete picture. The LTV calculator needs the correct rate per purity.

setup.persona: 50-year-old male, Seed Grower, rural Bhilwara, Rajasthan

user_turns.content: What's today's gold rate? I'm pledging 22 karat ornaments for a loan.

get_gold_rate._comment: FILTER TRAP: customer asks for 22k rate. get_gold_rate returns a flat object per purity_karat. Querying only 22k gives the 22k rate (Rs 5,800/g) but hides the 24k rate (Rs 6,250/g). A model that queries both purities gives a complete picture. The 24k rate matters because the customer's gold may include 24k items.
Must query 22k rate. The filter trap: querying only 22k hides the 24k rate. A thorough model queries both or at least notes that rates vary by purity and offers to look up 24k as well.

gold.expected_resolution: The customer asks for 22 karat gold rate. Today's 22k rate is Rs 5,800 per gram. The assistant should provide this AND note that rates vary by purity — 24k, 22k, and 18k have different rates — and offer to look up other purities if the customer has mixed-karat items. Reporting only the 22k rate without mentioning that other purities have different rates fails the disclosure standard.

judge_gate.axis_gate_rule: reports 22k gold rate (Rs 5,800/g) AND proactively notes that rates differ by purity and offers to provide other purity rates. Reporting only the 22k figure without the purity-rate caveat fails.
